# Bailiwick Sage 500 knowledge pack (portable edition)

**What this is.** Working knowledge of Bailiwick's Sage 500 ERP database (`MAS500_app`), written for
the Oracle Fusion finance conversion and the retirement of Sage. It is plain Markdown and T-SQL with
no dependency on any one assistant or tool.

**How to use it.**

- *With an AI assistant:* give this whole file as system instructions, project knowledge, a custom
  instruction file or an attached document. Tell the assistant how it reaches the database (any SQL
  Server client, or a query tool it has been given).
- *As a person:* read Part 1, then go to the part that fits the task. Part 6 is runnable SQL.
- *With Claude:* use the packaged skill in `skills/bailiwick-sage500/` instead; it carries the same
  content split into files that load on demand.

**Parts.** 1 Core rules · 2 Data model · 3 Custom objects · 4 Fusion conversion · 5 Retirement ·
6 Query library

**Instructions to an assistant reading this.** Treat Part 1 as rules. Before writing SQL, check the
table and column names in Part 2 or against the live catalog. Prefer adapting a query from Part 6 to
writing one from nothing. Figures in this document describe the 2026-11-13 snapshot; re-run the query
before a decision rests on a number. Never output passwords, bank account numbers or taxpayer IDs.

# Part 1. Core rules



Bailiwick Services runs its business on Sage 500 ERP, formerly MAS 500. A copy of that database now
sits beside the ePlus legacy databases, and the first leg of the move to Oracle Fusion is finance.
This skill lets you answer questions against that copy correctly on the first attempt, tell standard
Sage from the customisation layered on it over twenty years, and turn what you find into conversion
and retirement decisions.

## Connect

| | |
|---|---|
| MCP source | `Bailiwick-SAGE-Database` on the `aix-greenlight` server (`run_query`, `describe_table`, `start_extract`) |
| Database | `MAS500_app`, SQL Server 2022, **compatibility level 100**, schema `dbo`, about 128 GB |
| Access | Read-only. Object names are visible; view, procedure and trigger **source code is not** |
| Snapshot | Data runs through 2026-11-13. It is a restored copy, so it does not move |

With any other SQL client the same T-SQL applies; only the connection differs.

## Five rules that prevent wrong answers

1. **Filter to company `BDS`.** One database holds twelve companies. `BDS` (Bailiwick Services, LLC)
   is the operating company. `BEL`, `BMH` and `UTH` have no activity after 2018, `XBD` is a test company,
   and `CAD`, `COA`, `CON`, `DKS`, `SGE`, `SLS`, `SOA` are Sage demo data. An unfiltered count is wrong.
2. **Join on surrogate keys, show natural IDs.** Every entity has an integer `...Key` and a
   human `...ID` or `...No`. Join `VendKey`, `CustKey`, `GLAcctKey`; display `VendID`, `CustID`,
   `GLAcctNo`. Detail tables often carry no `CompanyID`, so reach it through the header or the account.
3. **Never guess a status code.** Decode it from `tsmListValidation` joined to `tsmLocalString`
   (query 1 in Part 6, "Query library"). `Status = 1` is Open for a voucher and Active for a vendor.
4. **GL balances are cumulative.** `tglAcctHist.BegBal` is filled only in period 1. A balance is the
   period-1 `BegBal` plus the sum of `DebitAmt - CreditAmt` through the period you want. In
   `tglTransaction`, a positive `PostAmtHC` is a debit.
5. **Write for compatibility level 100.** `STRING_AGG ... WITHIN GROUP`, `STRING_SPLIT` and
   `TRY_CONVERT` fail here (tested). Use `STUFF(... FOR XML PATH(''))` to aggregate strings and `CASE`
   with `ISNUMERIC` or `ISDATE` to guard conversions. `IIF`, `FORMAT`, `CONCAT`, `EOMONTH`,
   `OFFSET/FETCH` and window functions work. `char` columns are space padded, so `RTRIM` what you display.

## Fiscal calendar

The year was reshaped when ePlus acquired the business, and any period-based work must respect it.

| Fiscal year | Dates | Periods |
|---|---|---|
| 2005 to 2023 | calendar year | 12 |
| 2024 | 2024-01-01 to 2024-08-18 | 8, the last one short |
| 2025 | 2024-08-19 to 2025-03-31 | 8, the first one short |
| 2026 onward | 1 April to 31 March | 12 |

`FiscYear` is a `char` column. Fiscal 2027 period 8 (November 2026) is the open period in the snapshot.
Always take dates from `tglFiscalPeriod`; never derive a period from a calendar month.

## Read the reference that fits the task

| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| Write or explain a query; table, key and status detail | Part 2, "Data model" |
| Start from SQL that has already been run against this database | Part 6, "Query library" |
| Decide whether an object is standard, custom, third party or dead | Part 3, "Custom objects" |
| Scope, extract, map or reconcile a conversion to Oracle Fusion | Part 4, "Fusion conversion" |
| Plan archival, interface cut-over and switching Sage off | Part 5, "Retirement" |

## How to work

- **Verify before you assert.** Describe the table, run the query with `TOP`, then widen it. The
  references record what was true in the November 2026 snapshot; re-run anything a decision rests on.
- **Reconcile every extract.** A conversion extract is finished when its total ties to the general
  ledger control account, and not before. The method and the known variance are in
  Part 4, "Fusion conversion".
- **Use `start_extract` for whole tables.** `tglTransaction` has 29.9 million rows. Filter by
  `FiscYear` and company before anything else.
- **Say what you cannot see.** Module source is hidden from this login. Describe a custom view by its
  columns and say that its logic needs a definition export from the Bailiwick DBA.
- **Leave secrets alone.** Do not select `tsmUser.Password`, `tsmUser.DBPassword`,
  `tsmSiteProfile.AppRolePassword` or its key columns, `tcnConfig_rkl.RunAsPwd`,
  `tapVendAddr.BankAcctNo`, `tapVendAddr.BankRoutingTrnstNo` or `tapVendor.TaxPayerID` unless the task
  is the supplier bank or tax conversion itself, and then write them to the extract, never to chat.
- **Distrust cross-database synonyms.** All 101 point at databases that were not restored with this
  copy, and they raise error 5313. Views built on them fail too.

# Part 2. Data model


Everything here was read from `MAS500_app` in November 2026. Row counts are for the whole database
unless a company is named.

## Contents

1. Platform and version
2. Naming conventions
3. Companies
4. Shared patterns: keys, batches, transaction types, addresses, audit columns
5. General Ledger
6. Accounts Payable
7. Accounts Receivable
8. Cash Management
9. Project Accounting
10. Status and code decodes
11. Data quality notes

## 1. Platform and version

- SQL Server 2022 Standard, database `MAS500_app`, compatibility level 100, collation
  `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS` (case-insensitive).
- `tsmVersionControl` reports the core modules (SM, CI, GL, AP, AR, IM, SO, CM, MC, PO) at **7.70.0**.
  The newest `tsmDBHistory` row reads 7.80. Treat the product as Sage 500 ERP 7.7x and confirm the
  marketing release with Bailiwick IT before quoting it.
- Object waves, visible in `sys.objects.create_date`, tell the upgrade story: initial build
  2005-04-26, warehouse add-on 2006-11-12, upgrades 2008-07-26, 2013-12-27, 2015-03-27 and
  2019-04-05/06, an operations add-on 2015-06-30, and warehouse-system work 2025-02-18 to 2025-02-23.
  An object created on any other day is almost certainly custom.
- Modules active for `BDS`: SM, CI, GL, AP, AR, IM, SO, CM, PO, WM, PA, CZ (Customizer), DA, DP, EX,
  BA, BE, NA, IN, O2, OA. Multicurrency (MC), Manufacturing (MF) and Payroll (PR) are not active.

## 2. Naming conventions

| Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `t<mod><Name>` | Table. `<mod>` is a two-letter module: `gl`, `ap`, `ar`, `cm`, `ci`, `sm`, `im`, `so`, `po` |
| `tPA#####`, `tPA<Name>`, `pa<mod><Name>` | Project Accounting tables, with their own Hungarian columns (`intJobKey`, `chrJobNumber`, `numJTDActualCost`) |
| `v<mod>...`, `vdv...`, `vlu...` | Views: module views, Business Insights data views, lookup views |
| `sp<mod>...`, `fn...` | Procedures and functions |
| `tI_`, `tU_`, `tD_<table>` | Insert, update and delete triggers that enforce Sage's referential integrity |
| `...Wrk` | Report work table. Contents are leftovers from the last report run. **Never a source of truth** |
| `...Log` | Posting or change log. Useful as audit evidence, not for balances |
| `tPend...` (`tapPendVoucher`, `tarPendInvoice`) | Entered but **unposted** documents |
| `Stg...` | Data Migrator staging tables, nearly all empty |
| `txx...` | Seed and template data shipped by Sage |
| a suffix after an underscore | Custom or third party. See Part 3 |

## 3. Companies

`tsmCompany` holds twelve rows. Only one matters for conversion.

| CompanyID | Name | Standing |
|---|---|---|
| `BDS` | Bailiwick Services, LLC | **Operating company.** USD, single currency. Postings through 2026-11-12 |
| `BEL` | Palmetto, LLC | 41 vouchers, last in 2018. Fiscal years end at 2018 |
| `UTH` | Ubiquitous Technology Holding, LLC | 323 vouchers, last in 2018 |
| `BMH` | Bailiwick Management Holdings | Chart of accounts only, no transactions |
| `XBD` | CRP Bailiwick Test Company | Conference-room-pilot test data from 2005 and 2006 |
| `CAD`, `COA`, `CON`, `DKS`, `SGE`, `SLS`, `SOA` | Sage demonstration companies | `DemoData` is set. Ignore |

`BEL`, `UTH` and `BMH` are a retention question (do their ledgers need archiving?), not a conversion one.

## 4. Shared patterns

**Keys.** Surrogate integer keys are issued from `tciSurrogateKey`. They are unique per table across
all companies, so a join on a key never needs `CompanyID`, but a filter does.

**Batches.** Every posted document belongs to a batch: `tciBatchLog` (`BatchKey`, `BatchID`,
`BatchType`, `Status`, `PostDate`, `PostUserID`, `SourceCompanyID`). `Status` 6 is Posted and 4 is
Balanced. `BDS` carries roughly 609,000 batches at status 4, mostly system-created shipment and
invoice batches; do not read them as an unposted backlog without checking the pending tables.

**Transaction types.** `TranType` is a number whose leading digits are the module: 3xx GL, 4xx AP,
5xx AR, 7xx IM, 8xx SO, 11xx PO. `tciTranType` holds the definition, `tciTranTypeCompany` the
two-letter `TranTypeID` per company (`IN`, `CM`, `DM`, `CK`, `EF`, `CR`), and the description is
`tsmLocalString.LocalText` joined on `tciTranType.TranDescStrNo` with `LanguageID = 1033`.

| TranType | Meaning | | TranType | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 303 | General journal | | 501 | AR invoice |
| 401 | AP invoice (voucher) | | 502 | AR credit memo |
| 402 | AP debit memo | | 503 | AR debit memo |
| 403 | AP credit memo | | 511 | Cash receipt |
| 411 | AP check | | 512 | Write-off |
| 416 | AP EFT | | 514 | Receipt reversal |
| 417 | AP other payment | | 516 | Refund check |
| 810 | Customer shipment | | 1110 | PO receipt |

**Document numbers.** `TranNo` is the number, `TranID` is the number with the type appended
(`3641458-IN`). On an AP voucher `TranNo` and `TranID` carry the **supplier's invoice number** and
`VouchNo` is Bailiwick's internal voucher number.

**Addresses and contacts.** `tciAddress` (13.1 million rows) is shared by every module and joined by
`AddrKey`. A vendor's addresses are in `tapVendAddr` and a customer's in `tarCustAddr`; both are
extension rows keyed by the same `AddrKey`. Contacts are in `tciContact` by `CntctKey`.

**Audit columns.** `CreateDate`, `CreateUserID`, `UpdateDate`, `UpdateUserID` and `CreateType`
(1 Standard, 2 Import, 7 Migrate, 8 Warehouse Automation) sit on most master and header tables.
`UpdateCounter` is an optimistic-lock counter, not a version of business meaning.

**User fields.** `UserFld1` to `UserFld4` on master tables are free columns whose labels are defined
per company in `tciUserField` (join `tciEntity` on `EntityType` for the host table). The labels in use
for `BDS` are listed in Part 3.

## 5. General Ledger

| Table | Rows | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tglAccount` | 3,834 (347 for BDS, 194 active) | Account. `GLAcctKey`, `GLAcctNo`, `Description`, `Status`, `NaturalAcctKey` |
| `tglNaturalAcct` | 1,607 | Natural account, carrying `AcctTypeKey` and `AcctGroupKey` |
| `tglAcctType`, `tglAcctGroup`, `tglAcctCategory` | 228 / 182 / 108 | Classification. BDS has 19 types, 19 groups and nine categories |
| `tglSegment`, `tglSegmentCode`, `tglAcctSegment` | 34 / 1,714 / 13,308 | Segment definitions, values, and the value of each segment per account |
| `tglAcctRef`, `tglAcctRefGroup` | 81 / 17 | Account reference codes (74 for BDS) |
| `tglFiscalYear`, `tglFiscalPeriod` | 87 / 1,077 | Calendar, with `StartDate`, `EndDate`, `Status`, and per-module locks |
| `tglAcctHist` | 39,957 | Period balances: `BegBal`, `DebitAmt`, `CreditAmt` by `FiscYear`, `FiscPer`, `GLAcctKey` |
| `tglAcctHistAcctRef` | 29,327 | The same activity split by account reference code |
| `tglTransaction` | 29,897,673 | Posted journal lines |
| `tglJournal` | 172 | Journal definitions (`JrnlID` such as `JE`) |
| `tglBudget`, `tglBudgetType` | 10,440 / 16 | Budgets. BDS has **no** budget rows for fiscal 2027 |
| `tglRecurJournal`, `tglRecurJrnlDetl` | 25 / 3,296 | Recurring journal templates |

**The BDS chart is one segment.** The account mask is `999999`: a six-digit natural account and
nothing else. There is no company, department or location segment in the account number.

**Account reference codes do the work of a department segment.** `tglOptions.AcctRefUsage = 1` for BDS,
and journal lines carry `AcctRefKey` pointing at codes such as `Acct` (Accounting), `Admin`, `IT` and
`AB` (Arboretum Warehouse). About 5,700 of the 1.1 million fiscal-2027 lines carry one. They are the
only analytic dimension in the ledger, so they matter to the Fusion chart of accounts design.

**Account categories for BDS:** 1 Asset, 2 Liability, 3 Equity, 4 Revenue, 5 Cost of Sales,
6 Other Income and Expense, 7 Income Tax, 8 Expense, 9 Non-Financial.

**Sign and balance rules.**
- `tglTransaction.PostAmtHC` is in home currency; positive is a debit and negative a credit. `PostAmt`
  is the transaction-currency amount. For BDS the two are equal, because everything is USD.
- `tglAcctHist.BegBal` is populated in **period 1 only** and is zero in every later period. Income
  statement accounts open each year at zero.
- Ending balance = period-1 `BegBal` + sum of (`DebitAmt` - `CreditAmt`) for periods 1 to N.
- Proven on the snapshot: the trial balance for fiscal 2027 through period 8 sums to 0.000, and
  debits in `tglTransaction` equal `tglAcctHist.DebitAmt` for a tested period.

**Tracing a journal line to its source.** `SourceModuleNo` names the module (3 GL, 4 AP, 5 AR, 7 IM,
8 SO, 11 PO; the full list is in `tsmModuleDef`). `TranType` and `TranKey` identify the source document:
for `TranType` 401 the `TranKey` is a `tapVoucher.VoucherKey`, for 501 a `tarInvoice.InvcKey`, for 511 a
`tarCustPmt.CustPmtKey`. `BatchKey` leads to `tciBatchLog`, `JrnlKey` and `JrnlNo` to the journal.

Where fiscal 2027 volume comes from (BDS, April to mid-November 2026): AR invoices 509,000 lines,
SO shipments 431,000, AP invoices 80,000, PO receipts 20,000, cash receipts 14,000, EFT payments
11,000, and only 4,200 manual general journal lines. The ledger is fed almost wholly by subledgers.

BDS position in the snapshot:
- 1,933 active and 3,546 inactive suppliers. **882** active suppliers had a voucher in the 24 months to
  November 2026, and 278 have an open one.
- 5,205 open vouchers and debit memos, net **8,218,251.65**. Of that, 8,214,959.78 sits in classes
  whose control account is `200000 AP`, and it ties to the general ledger to the cent. The other
  3,291.87 belongs to class `Int Tech`, which posts to `600500`.
- Nine supplier classes hold open items: Labor, Equip & Mat, Lift, Freight, Other, Employee,
  Utilities, Int Tech and Customer.
- 132 active suppliers are flagged for 1099 reporting, 451 have a taxpayer ID, and 1,612 supplier
  addresses carry bank account details for EFT.

## 7. Accounts Receivable

| Table | Rows | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tarCustomer` | 88,804 (88,072 BDS) | Customer. `CustKey`, `CustID`, `CustName`, `Status`, `CustClassKey`, `NationalAcctLevelKey` |
| `tarCustAddr` | 3,154,604 | Customer address extension. One customer has 2,424 addresses |
| `tarCustClass` | 48 | Class. Carries the **AR control account** in `AcctsRecAcctKey` |
| `tarNationalAcct`, `tarNationalAcctLevel`, `tarNationalAcctMember` | 733 / 72,040 / 87,685 | National account hierarchy |
| `tarInvoice` | 630,709 | Posted invoice header. `Status` 1 Open, 2 Closed, 3 Void |
| `tarInvoiceDetl`, `tarInvoiceLineDist` | 12,219,576 each | Lines and their GL distribution (`SalesAcctKey`) |
| `tarCustPmt` | 52,147 | Receipts, write-offs, reversals and refunds |
| `tarCustPmtAppl`, `tarInvoiceAppl` | 617,844 / 662,993 | Applications, seen from each side |
| `tarPendInvoice` | 150 (84 BDS) | Unposted invoices |
| `tarRecurInvoice` | 2,564 | Recurring invoice templates |
| `tarSalesperson` | 56 | Salespeople |

**Read the customer master with care.** BDS has 87,830 active customers, and nearly all of them
belong to a national account, yet only **52** were invoiced in the 24 months to November 2026 and
only 29 have an open invoice. The shape of the data (733 national accounts, 87,685 members, up to
2,424 addresses on one customer) suggests that most customer rows are individual service sites and
that the national account is the commercial customer. That reading is an inference to confirm with
Bailiwick finance. Either way, converting the table row for row would create tens of thousands of
dead Fusion accounts.

**Customer classes are people.** The classes holding open items are named for account managers
(`MWolter`, `KHexum`, `SMuschewske`, `BLange` and others), and every one posts to control account
`101000 A/R`. The class is a reporting attribute here, not an accounting one.

BDS position in the snapshot: 4,406 open invoices and credit memos, net **22,980,151.60**, and 39
receipts with 483,785.98 unapplied. Subledger net 22,496,365.62 against general ledger `101000` of
21,585,640.46, a difference of **910,725.16**. Nearly all of it is manual: 504 general journal lines
posted straight to `101000` between 2006 and 2026 net to -909,483.02, and one AP line adds 1,770.96.
That leaves about 3,013 unexplained. The control account has been adjusted by journal for years, so
the subledger, not the ledger, is the list of what customers owe.

## 8. Cash Management

`tcmBank` (14), `tcmCashAcct` (17, four for BDS, each mapped to a `GLAcctKey`), `tcmCashTran`
(230,040; `Status` 1 Outstanding, 2 Cleared, 3 Void), `tcmBankStatement` (146). AP payments and AR
receipts link to cash through `CashAcctKey` and `CashTranKey`.

**Bank reconciliation is not kept up in Sage.** About 175,000 BDS cash transactions are still
`Outstanding`, including 84,542 checks back to 2009 and 68,966 EFT payments back to 2018. The status
column therefore says nothing about what has cleared the bank; reconciliation evidently happens
elsewhere. Do not build an outstanding-items list from `tcmCashTran`.

## 9. Project Accounting

Bailiwick is a project business, and Project Accounting runs through sales, purchasing and billing.

| Table | Rows | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `tPA00176` | 1,494 | Master project (`chrMasterJobNumber`) |
| `tPA00175` | 203,613 (201,693 BDS, **1,218 open**) | Project (`chrJobNumber`, `CustKey`, `OpenOrClosed`, job-to-date totals) |
| `tPA00125` | 5,017,247 | Project line: estimate, actual, committed and recognised amounts |
| `tPA00100` | 2,245,554 | Line detail |
| `tPAGLTranRef` | 3,490,312 | Project-to-GL posting reference |
| `tPA00007` | resources | Employees and their cost and charge rates |
| `paarInvcHdr`, `paarInvcLine`, `paapLine`, `papoLine` | 180,933 / 729,350 / 334,271 / 307,974 | Links from AR invoices, AP vouchers and PO lines to project lines |

`tarInvoiceDetl` also carries `ProjID` and `ProjClientID`. Projects are outside a finance-only first
leg unless Fusion Project Financials is in scope, but open AR and AP documents reference them, so
agree early whether the project number travels as an attribute.

## 11. Data quality notes

- **Impossible dates.** Closed AP vouchers carry `TranDate` values from 1900-01-01 to 2066-08-31. Bound
  every date filter at both ends, and prefer `PostDate` with `FiscYear` and `FiscPer` for period logic.
- **Padded text.** `char` columns such as `FiscYear`, `VendID` and `GLAcctNo` are space padded.
  Equality comparisons ignore the padding in SQL Server; exports and joins made outside it do not.
- **Duplicate identities.** Eleven BDS customers are also linked to a vendor (`tarCustomer.VendKey`).
- **Stored aging is stale by design.** `tapVendStatus` and `tarCustStatus` hold buckets as of their
  own `AgingDate`. Age from `DueDate` yourself.
- **Work tables look like data.** `tapAgedUnapplWrk` (6.1 million rows), `tarAgeInvUnApWrk` (12.5
  million) and `timPPInvtValLstWrk` (18.2 million) are report residue.

# Part 3. Custom objects


Twenty years of add-ons, reseller work and in-house reporting sit on top of standard Sage 500. This
file is the review of that layer: what exists, who appears to have built it, whether it is alive, and
what each piece means for the Fusion finance conversion and for retirement.

## Contents

1. How the review was done, and its limits
2. Origin tags
3. Finance-relevant customisations
4. Integrations and the systems behind them
5. In-house reporting views
6. Extension tables and user fields
7. Screen customisations
8. Backups, one-offs and debris
9. Counts at a glance
10. Re-running the review

## 1. Method and limits

Objects were classified from the SQL Server catalog by three signals: a suffix or prefix that marks an
author, a creation date outside Sage's install and upgrade waves (see Part 2), and row counts
with last-activity dates.

**The login cannot read module source.** `sys.sql_modules.definition` is NULL for all 1,482 views,
3,420 triggers, 209 procedures and 59 functions, and `sys.sql_expression_dependencies` is empty. Every
statement below about what an object *does* rests on its name, its columns and its data. Before a
custom view is rebuilt or a trigger's side effect is ruled out, ask the Bailiwick DBA for a script of
the definitions, or for `VIEW DEFINITION` on the database.

Only 178 stored procedures are visible, far fewer than a Sage 500 install carries, so the procedure
list is incomplete in this copy.

Vendor names against tags are the reviewer's reading. Those marked *unconfirmed* should be checked
with Bailiwick IT.

## 3. Finance-relevant customisations

These touch the ledger, payables or receivables, and each needs a decision in the first leg.

**Concur expense import (`_XPNS_rkl`, `tpaConcur...`, `tcnConfig_rkl`).** Files from Concur are loaded
as AP vouchers and project expenses. `tpaConcurLog_rkl` records 1,884 file downloads, the latest on
2026-11-12, with interface type `AP`. `tcnConfig_rkl` holds the file paths, the vendor class and offset
account used, a `SummarizeTrans` switch and a run-as credential (do not select `RunAsPwd`).
`tpaXRef_rkl` and `tpaColumnMap_rkl` hold the Concur-to-Sage cross-references. `idsVend_XPNS_RKL`
(258,383 rows) and `idsPmt_XPNS_RKL` (383,364) are change queues that feed vendors and payments back
to Concur. **Fusion impact:** this is a two-way interface that must be re-pointed at Fusion Payables,
and its cross-reference tables are a ready-made mapping source.

**Adaptive planning feed (`vAdaptiveGLAcctHist`, `vAdaptive500GLTrxn`).** Created in October 2019 and
edited in 2023. They expose period balances and journal lines with account category, group and type,
and four segment columns. They run in this copy. **Fusion impact:** a planning tool reads the ledger
through these; the feed needs a Fusion source before cut-over.

**GL transaction views (`VDVGLAccountTran_BW`, `vdvglAccountTran`, `vdvglAccountTran_RKL`).** Journal
lines with batch, journal, reference code, source document and, in the RKL version, the PO, receiver
and voucher keys behind each line. They are the model for a GL detail extract, and they are evidence
of what the finance team reports on today.

**Sales tax (`exactor_...`, `tarPendInvoice_Exactor`, `tciBatchLog_exactor`, `tciBatchTran_exactor`).**
Triggers `insertExactorTrigger`, `new_updateExactorTrigger` and `deleteExactorTrigger` on
`tarPendInvoice`, with `updateExactor_tciBatchLog` and `updateExactor_tciBatchTran`, are enabled, yet
the last Exactor transaction is dated January 2018. **Fusion impact:** none for conversion; confirm
how sales tax is calculated today, because this route is not it.

**AR invoice shadow tables (`tarInvoiceDetl_ERP`, `tarInvoiceLineDist_ERP`, `tarPendInvoice_ERP`).**
4.3 million, 4.3 million and 827,448 rows, with the same columns as the standard tables. They look
like a copy taken for an interface or an archive. **Do not extract from them.** The standard
`tarInvoiceDetl` (12.2 million rows) is the complete set.

**Custom triggers on supplier and payment tables.** `tR_tapVendor_idsVend_XPNS_rkl`,
`tR_tapVendAddr_idsVend_XPNS_rkl` and `tR_tciAddress_idsVend_XPNS_rkl` queue every supplier or
address change, and `tR_tapVendPmt_idsPmt_rkl` every payment, for the Concur feed. `BW_TransactionOverride`
(2019) sits on the shared `tciAddress` table. All are enabled. They do not change what is stored in
the finance tables as far as the catalog shows, but their source is unreadable here, so confirm it.

**Change auditing (standard Sage, switched on).** Triggers named `..._AppAudit` on `tapVendor`,
`tapVendAddr`, `tarCustomer`, `tarCustAddr`, `tarSalesperson`, `tciAddress`, `tglAccount`, `timItem`,
`timInventory` and `timItemDescription` were created by the 2019 upgrade and are Sage's own audit
feature, not custom work. `tciMaintAuditLog` holds 919,915 rows, the latest dated 2026-11-12. That log
is the audit trail for master-data changes and belongs in the archive.

**Fiscal calendar change.** `tsmAddonTask` chains `spapChangeFiscalCalendar`,
`sparChangeFiscalCalendar`, `spcmChangeFiscalCalendar` and `spimChangeFiscalCalendar` onto a GL task.
This is the machinery behind the 2024 year-end change, and it explains the two eight-period years.

**Supplier and customer extensions.** `tapVendorCustomData_SSS` and `tarCustomerCustomData_SSS` each
hold one row. Nothing to convert.

**Project accounting additions.** `tpaLogProjStatChange_sssi` (171,928 rows) logs project status
changes, `tpaProjHistory_sssi` (24,411) holds project history, and `tpaSOShipmentLink_MAG` (787,119)
with `tmag_tPASOLink` (793,996) link shipments to project lines. `tPA00125_ERPNotes` (275,049) holds
project line notes. Views `vdvPA...Postings_MAG` expose project postings by source. In scope only if
projects are.

# Part 4. Fusion conversion


This is the first leg: general ledger, payables, receivables and cash. The aim of this file is to
make every conversion object small, defensible and reconciled.

The Fusion targets named here are the standard file-based data import (FBDI) objects for each area.
They are the usual destination, not a statement of this engagement's design: check each against the
programme's conversion inventory and the Fusion release in use before building a template.

## Contents

1. Principles
2. Scope in numbers
3. Object by object
4. The chart of accounts problem
5. The calendar problem
6. Reconciliation
7. Extraction mechanics
8. Decisions for the business

## 1. Principles

- **Convert open items and balances, archive history.** Sage holds 1.07 million vouchers and 630,709
  invoices; about 5,200 and 4,400 of them are open. History belongs in the archive
  (Part 5), not in Fusion.
- **Convert what is used, not what exists.** Activity in the last 24 months is the test for master
  data. It cuts suppliers from 5,481 to under 1,000 and customers from 88,072 to a few dozen
  accounts plus the sites they need.
- **Company `BDS` only.** Every extract filters to it.
- **Tie to the ledger.** An extract is accepted when its total equals the control account balance
  for the same date, or when the difference is itemised.
- **Keep the Sage key.** Carry `VendKey`, `CustKey`, `VoucherKey`, `InvcKey` and `GLAcctKey` in a
  reference or descriptive field through staging, so that Fusion records trace back to the source.

## 2. Scope in numbers

| Account reference codes | 74 | to be decided | See section 4 |
| Suppliers | 5,481 (1,933 active) | about 900 | 882 active suppliers vouchered in 24 months, plus any with open items |
| Supplier sites | 8,485 addresses, all companies | sites of converted suppliers | Purchasing and remit-to addresses |
| Supplier bank accounts | 1,612 addresses with bank details | those of converted suppliers | EFT is the main payment method: 11,000 EFT lines against 330 check lines in fiscal 2027 |
| 1099 suppliers | 132 active | all | Carry form, box and type; year-to-date amounts if cut-over is mid calendar year |

## 3. Object by object

### Chart of accounts and balances

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `tglAccount`, `tglNaturalAcct`, `tglAcctType`, `tglAcctGroup`, `tglAcctCategory`, `tglAcctRef`, `tglAcctHist`, `tglAcctHistAcctRef` |
| Fusion target | Segment values and hierarchies import (`GL_SEGMENT_VALUES_INTERFACE`, `GL_SEGMENT_HIER_INTERFACE`); balances and journals through Journal Import (`GL_INTERFACE`) |
| Key rules | Balance = period-1 `BegBal` plus cumulative activity. Use `tglAcctHistAcctRef` when balances are needed by reference code. The retained earnings account is named in `tglOptions.RetainedEarnAcct` |
| Account type | `tglAcctCategory` gives Asset, Liability, Equity, Revenue and the expense groupings that set the Fusion account type |
| Watch for | Sage `Status` 3 (Deleted) accounts that still hold history; statistical accounts (`PostingType` 2 or 3) |

Bank accounts through the supplier bank account import (`IBY_TEMP_EXT_PAYEES`, `IBY_TEMP_EXT_BANK_ACCTS`, `IBY_TEMP_PMT_INSTR_USES`) |

| Watch for | Supplier class names (`Labor`, `Equip & Mat`, `Lift`, `Freight`, `Employee`, `Utilities`) are candidates for supplier type. Class `Employee` suggests expense reimbursements paid as supplier invoices; with Concur in place, decide whether those convert at all. Eleven customers are linked to a vendor |
| Sensitive | Bank account numbers, routing numbers and taxpayer IDs. Extract to a controlled file, never into a chat or a ticket |

### Open payables

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `tapVoucher` where `Status = 1`, with `tapVoucherDetl` and `tapVoucherLineDist` |
| Fusion target | Payables invoice import: `AP_INVOICES_INTERFACE`, `AP_INVOICE_LINES_INTERFACE` |
| Mapping notes | `TranNo` is the supplier invoice number; `VouchNo` is Sage's voucher number and makes a good reference. `TranDate` is the invoice date, `DueDate` and `PmtTermsKey` give terms, `BalanceHC` is the open amount. `TranType` 402 debit memos load as negative documents |
| Method | Load each open document for its **remaining balance** on a single line coded to a conversion clearing account, so that Fusion AP equals Sage AP on day one. Part-paid vouchers need this; reloading the original amount and the payments does not reconcile |

### Open receivables

| | |
|---|---|
| Source | `tarInvoice` where `Status = 1`; `tarCustPmt` where `UnappliedAmtHC <> 0` |
| Fusion target | AutoInvoice: `RA_INTERFACE_LINES_ALL`, `RA_INTERFACE_DISTRIBUTIONS_ALL`. Unapplied cash through the standard receipt import |
| Mapping notes | `TranID` or `TranNo` is the invoice number, `CustPONo` the customer PO, `BalanceHC` the open amount. `TranType` 502 credit memos load as credit transactions. The project is on the invoice lines (`tarInvoiceDetl.ProjID`) |
| Method | As for payables: one line per document for the remaining balance, coded to a clearing account |
| Watch for | Open invoices dating back to 2005; agree a write-off pass before conversion. 84 unposted invoices in `tarPendInvoice`. Sales tax on converted balances should not be recalculated in Fusion |

### Banks and cash

`tcmBank` and `tcmCashAcct` (with its `GLAcctKey`). Bank, branch and account are Fusion Cash
Management setup. BDS has four cash accounts: a primary checking account on GL `100000`, a payroll
account on `100002`, an older account on `100001` and a clearing pseudo-account.

Do not take outstanding items from Sage. Bank reconciliation is not maintained there: about 175,000
cash transactions back to 2008 still show as outstanding. The list of uncleared checks and deposits
at cut-over has to come from wherever finance reconciles the bank today.

### Reference data

Payment terms (`tciPaymentTerms`, with the due-date and discount options decoded in Part 2),
payment methods, sales tax schedules (`tciSTaxSchedule`, `tciSTaxCode`) and currencies are
configuration. Extract them as mapping tables, not as loads.

## 4. The chart of accounts problem

Sage BDS has a single six-digit segment. Fusion will have a multi-segment chart. Every other segment
must therefore be **derived**, and the source for derivation is thin:

- **Company** comes from `CompanyID`. All of BDS is one legal entity value.
- **Department or cost centre** can come only from account reference codes, which appear on a small
  share of lines (about 5,700 of 1.1 million in fiscal 2027). Lines without one need a default.
- **Project, location or line of business** are not in the ledger at all. They exist on subledger
  documents (project on invoice and voucher lines) and would have to be joined in.

Build the mapping as a table of Sage `GLAcctNo` plus `AcctRefCode` to a full Fusion combination,
profile it with Part 6 section 2, and have finance sign it before any balance is loaded. Agree
at the same time whether history is converted at account level only.

## 5. The calendar problem

Sage's years are calendar years to 2023, then an eight-period year ending 2024-08-18, an eight-period
year ending 2025-03-31, then April-to-March. Fusion's calendar for the entity will be ePlus's.

- Never map `FiscPer` to a Fusion period by number. Map by `tglFiscalPeriod.EndDate`.
- Period 8 of fiscal 2024 (18 days) and period 1 of fiscal 2025 (13 days) both fall in August 2024.
  If monthly history is loaded, decide whether they combine into one Fusion period.
- Decide how much history Fusion needs: opening balances only, the current year by period, or
  comparatives. Each further year multiplies the mapping risk in section 4.

## 6. Reconciliation

Run in this order. Each step has a query in Part 6.

1. **Ledger integrity.** The trial balance sums to zero for the cut-over period. (Verified: 0.000 for
   fiscal 2027 period 8.)
2. **Activity integrity.** Debits in `tglTransaction` equal `tglAcctHist.DebitAmt` for the period.
   (Verified for fiscal 2027 period 7.)
3. **AP to GL.** Open vouchers by control account against the GL balance of that account. (Verified:
   8,214,959.78 on both sides for `200000`.)
4. **AR to GL.** Open invoices less unapplied receipts against `101000`. **The subledger is
   910,725.16 higher than the ledger.** Query 6e shows why: 504 general journal lines posted directly
   to `101000` from 2006 to 2026 net to -909,483.02, and one AP line adds 1,770.96, leaving about
   3,013 to find. In effect the ledger carries a manual reduction of receivables (a reserve or
   accumulated corrections) inside the control account. Finance must decide before conversion whether
   that amount is written off against specific invoices, moved to a reserve account, or converted as
   a separate balance. Fusion will not tolerate a control account that differs from its subledger.
5. **Extract to source.** Row count and amount of each extract against the query that defined it.
6. **Load to extract.** Fusion interface and base table totals against the extract.
7. **Fusion subledger to Fusion GL** after the conversion journals post.

Keep the output of every step with its run date. It is the audit evidence for the conversion.

## 7. Extraction mechanics

- Extract with one statement per object and stable ordering, so that reruns compare cleanly.
- Use `start_extract` (or any bulk export) for anything over a few thousand rows; the query tool caps
  interactive results.
- `RTRIM` every `char` column, and convert dates with `CONVERT(varchar(10), col, 120)`.
- Strip or escape embedded delimiters and line breaks in free text such as `TranCmnt` and addresses.
- This copy is static. Final extracts must come from production, or from a copy taken after the
  final Sage close, with the reconciliation re-run on that copy.

## 8. Decisions for the business

1. **What is a customer in Fusion?** With 87,830 active rows and 52 billed, choose between converting
   national accounts as customer accounts with sites beneath, converting only billed customers and
   their open-item sites, or another model. This decision sizes the whole receivables conversion.
2. **How are the missing chart segments derived**, and what is the default when a line has no
   reference code?
3. **How much GL history**, and are the two August 2024 stub periods merged?
4. **The AR variance** of 910,725.16, built from manual journals to the control account: write off,
   reclassify to a reserve, or convert separately, and who owns it?
5. **Old open receivables** from 2005 onward: write off before conversion, or convert?
6. **Dormant companies** `BEL`, `UTH` and `BMH`: archive only, or bring closing balances?
7. **Employee suppliers and Concur**: do reimbursed employees become Fusion suppliers?
8. **Projects**: is the project number carried on converted open items, and where?

# Part 5. Retirement


Conversion moves the open position into Fusion. Retirement is everything else: keeping what must be
kept, cutting every interface, and switching the system off without losing the ability to answer an
auditor. Finance goes first, and Sage keeps running for the other legs, so retirement here is staged.

## Contents

1. Staged retirement
2. What must be archived
3. What can be left behind
4. Interfaces to cut or re-point
5. Reports to replace
6. Sensitive data
7. Access and operations
8. Readiness checklist

## 1. Staged retirement

Sales orders, purchasing, inventory, warehousing and projects all post to the Sage ledger: in fiscal
2027, shipments and receipts produced about 450,000 GL lines and manual journals only 4,200. Moving
finance first therefore leaves a live operational Sage whose accounting still has to reach a ledger.

| Stage | State of Sage | Key question |
|---|---|---|
| A. Finance cut-over | GL, AP, AR and CM frozen for new entry; operations continue | How do Sage's operational postings (shipments, receipts, inventory adjustments, AR invoices raised from shipments) reach Fusion? A summarised journal feed from `tglTransaction` by source module is the usual bridge |
| B. Later legs | Modules switched off as each moves | Which module's last posting closes which Sage period? |
| C. Read-only | No entry of any kind | Is every interface in section 4 stopped or re-pointed? |
| D. Archive and decommission | Database retained as an archive, application removed | Is the archive queryable without Sage installed? |

Agree the bridge in stage A before cut-over. It is the most commonly missed piece of a finance-first
programme.

## 2. What must be archived

The database is about 128 GB. Keep the whole thing as the system of record for history; these are the
tables an auditor, a tax authority or a customer dispute will actually need.

| Area | Tables | Size |
|---|---|---|
| General ledger | `tglTransaction`, `tglAcctHist`, `tglAcctHistAcctRef`, `tglAccount`, `tglFiscalPeriod`, `tglJournal` | 29.9 million journal lines, 2003 to 2026 |
| Payables | `tapVoucher`, `tapVoucherDetl`, `tapVoucherLineDist`, `tapVendPmt`, `tapVendPmtAppl`, `tapVendor`, `tapVendAddr` | 1.07 million vouchers, 186,148 payments |
| Receivables | `tarInvoice`, `tarInvoiceDetl`, `tarInvoiceLineDist`, `tarCustPmt`, `tarCustPmtAppl`, `tarCustomer`, `tarCustAddr` | 630,709 invoices, 12.2 million lines |
| Sales tax | `tciSTaxTran`, `tciSTaxCodeTran`, `tciSTaxDetail` | 20.3 million and 21.4 million rows |
| 1099 | `tapVend1099Hist`, `tapVend1099Bal`, the 1099 columns on vouchers and payment applications | |
| Cash | `tcmCashTran`, `tcmBankStatement` | 230,040 transactions |
| Projects | `tPA00175`, `tPA00176`, `tPA00125`, `tPA00100`, `tPAGLTranRef` | 203,613 projects |
| Audit trail | `tciMaintAuditLog`, `tciBatchLog`, the `...Log` tables per module | 919,915 master-data changes |
| Shared | `tciAddress`, `tciContact`, `tsmCompany`, `tsmUser` (without password columns), `tsmListValidation`, `tsmLocalString`, `tciTranType` | Needed to decode everything else |

**Keep the decode tables with the data.** Status numbers and transaction types are meaningless
without `tsmListValidation`, `tsmLocalString`, `tciTranType` and `tsmModuleDef`.

**Keep the custom view definitions.** The Bailiwick views encode how the business read its own data.
Script them from production, where the source is readable, and store the script with the archive.

Retention periods are a legal and tax decision for ePlus finance; this file does not set them. Note
that data reaches back to 2003, and that the dormant companies `BEL`, `UTH` and `BMH` and the test
company `XBD` share the database.

Archive shape, in rising order of effort: keep the SQL Server database read-only on supported
infrastructure; export the tables above to an analytical store with the decode tables flattened in;
or do both, with the database kept offline as the legal copy. Whatever is chosen, prove it by
answering three questions from the archive alone: a supplier's payment history, a customer invoice
with its lines and tax, and a GL account's activity for a past period.

## 3. What can be left behind

Sage demonstration companies; `...Wrk` report work tables (tens of millions of rows of residue); the
empty `Stg...` staging tables; the dated backup tables from February 2025; the `aspnet_...` tables;
unused manufacturing and configurator tables; `tsmTraceTable_20061110_SSSI`; the `_ERP` shadow copies
of AR invoice lines once it is confirmed that nothing reads them. The full list is in
Part 3, section 8.

## 4. Interfaces to cut or re-point

Each of these writes to or reads from Sage today. Retirement is not complete while any is running.

| Interface | Direction | Evidence it is live | Action for the finance leg |
|---|---|---|---|
| Concur expenses | In (vouchers, project expenses) and out (vendors, payments) | File log to 2026-11-12 | Re-point to Fusion Payables. Reuse `tpaXRef_rkl` as the mapping source |
| Planning feed (`vAdaptive...` views) | Out (GL balances and lines) | Views maintained to 2023 | Give the planning tool a Fusion source |
| Integration hub (`Prod_MAS500Integration`) | Both (master data stages, invoice archive) | Synonyms; shipment log to 2026-11-12 | Identify each stage's owner; move the finance ones |
| Fieldpoint field service | Both (requisitions, projects, items) | Synonyms from 2023; a recurring journal entry references it | Confirm what posts to finance and how it will reach Fusion |
| Change-data-capture replication | Out (whole database) | `attrep_truncation_safeguard`, 2024 | Find the downstream warehouse or lake; its finance reports change source |
| FRx reporting | Out | `frl_...` tables from 2005 | Confirm it is unused; replace with Fusion reporting |
| mobe3, Modula, ShipExec, UPS, ServiceNow | Both | Various | Supply-chain leg. They keep running against Sage until then |
| Exactor sales tax | Out | **None since January 2018** | Already dead. Drop the five triggers at decommission |
| Bank files | Out (ACH), in (statements) | `tapACHLog` (610 rows), `tcmBankStatement` (146) | Re-establish payment and statement formats in Fusion |
| Bank reconciliation tool | Unknown | Sage shows about 175,000 cash transactions never cleared, so reconciliation is done elsewhere | Find it; it reads Sage payments and receipts today |

There are no SQL Server linked servers in this copy, and every synonym target is missing, so
dependency checking must be repeated on the production server, where the SQL Agent jobs, linked
servers and the integration database can be seen.

## 5. Reports to replace

The inventory of what users run is the set of custom views (Part 3, section 5), the 70
non-system Business Insights data views in `tsmDataView`, the financial statement definitions in
`tglFSReport` (50 reports with their rows and columns), and whatever SSRS or Crystal reports sit
outside the database. For each finance report decide: replaced by a Fusion standard report, rebuilt
(OTBI or BI Publisher), served from the archive, or retired. `tglFSReport`, `tglFSRow` and
`tglFSColumn` are worth extracting early, because they document the statement layout the business
expects from Fusion.

## 6. Sensitive data

The database contains material that should not travel into extracts or an archive without control:

- `tapVendAddr.BankAcctNo` and `BankRoutingTrnstNo` (1,612 BDS supplier addresses), `tapVendor.TaxPayerID`.
- `tsmUser.Password` and `DBPassword`; `tsmSiteProfile.AppRolePassword`, unlock and registration keys.
- `tcnConfig_rkl.RunAsUser` and `RunAsPwd` (the Concur interface's run-as credential).
- `tcmCashAcct` bank account and ACH origin identifiers.
- Customer and supplier contact details in `tciContact` and `tciAddress`.

For an archive, mask or drop the credential columns, restrict the banking and tax columns, and rotate
any credential that has been copied out of production, including the application role password, which
is present in this copy.

## 7. Access and operations

- 115 Sage users exist in `tsmUser`. Review them against current staff before granting archive access.
- This copy's login is read-only and cannot see module source. An archive reader needs no more.
- Once read-only, disable SQL Agent jobs that post, import or purge, and keep the purge settings in
  `tglOptions` and its sibling option tables from deleting history.

## 8. Readiness checklist

1. Final Sage period closed; trial balance sums to zero; AP and AR tie to the ledger.
2. No pending documents: `tapPendVoucher`, `tarPendInvoice`, `tapPendVendPmt`, `tarPendCustPmt` empty,
   and no batch at status In Use, Out of Balance or Interrupted that anyone intends to post.
3. Conversion loads reconciled and signed (see Part 4, section 6).
4. Bridge for operational postings running and reconciled for at least one period.
5. Every interface in section 4 stopped, re-pointed or explicitly accepted as still running.
6. Every finance report in section 5 has a disposition.
7. Custom definitions scripted from production and stored.
8. Archive built, the three test questions answered from it, credentials masked.
9. Users moved to read-only, then removed.
10. Retention owner and destruction date recorded.

# Part 6. Query library

```sql
/* ============================================================================
   Bailiwick Sage 500 (MAS500_app) - validated query library
   Dialect : T-SQL, written for database compatibility level 100
             (no STRING_AGG WITHIN GROUP, STRING_SPLIT or TRY_CONVERT)
   Company : BDS is the operating company. Change @-style literals to suit.
   Status  : every statement below ran against the 2026-11-13 snapshot.
             Run one statement at a time; most query tools accept only one.
   Literals to change: 'BDS', fiscal year '2027', period 8, as-of date
             '2026-11-13', and the activity window start '2024-11-01'.
   ============================================================================ */


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   1. DECODE A STATUS OR CODE COLUMN
   Never guess what a number means. Ask the Sage dictionary.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT lv.TableName, lv.ColumnName, lv.DBValue, RTRIM(ls.LocalText) AS Meaning
FROM   tsmListValidation lv
JOIN   tsmLocalString ls ON ls.StringNo = lv.StringNo AND ls.LanguageID = 1033
WHERE  lv.TableName = 'tapVoucher'          -- table
  AND  lv.ColumnName = 'Status'             -- column
ORDER BY lv.DBValue;

-- Transaction types with their descriptions and per-company two-letter IDs
SELECT tt.TranType, RTRIM(d.ModuleID) AS Module, RTRIM(ttc.TranTypeID) AS TranTypeID,
       RTRIM(ls.LocalText) AS Description
FROM   tciTranType tt
LEFT JOIN tsmModuleDef d        ON d.ModuleNo = tt.ModuleNo
LEFT JOIN tciTranTypeCompany ttc ON ttc.TranType = tt.TranType AND ttc.CompanyID = 'BDS'
LEFT JOIN tsmLocalString ls     ON ls.StringNo = tt.TranDescStrNo AND ls.LanguageID = 1033
ORDER BY tt.TranType;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   2. CHART OF ACCOUNTS
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- 2a. Accounts with their classification and last period of activity
SELECT RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo)        AS GLAcctNo,
       RTRIM(a.Description)     AS Description,
       a.Status,                                  -- 1 Active, 2 Inactive, 3 Deleted
       a.PostingType,                             -- 1 Financial, 2 Statistical, 3 Both
       RTRIM(cat.Description)   AS Category,
       RTRIM(grp.AcctGroupID)   AS AcctGroup,
       RTRIM(typ.AcctTypeID)    AS AcctType,
       act.LastFiscYear, act.Periods
FROM   tglAccount a
JOIN   tglNaturalAcct n     ON n.NaturalAcctKey = a.NaturalAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tglAcctType typ   ON typ.AcctTypeKey = n.AcctTypeKey
LEFT JOIN tglAcctGroup grp  ON grp.AcctGroupKey = n.AcctGroupKey
LEFT JOIN tglAcctCategory cat ON cat.AcctCategoryKey = typ.AcctCategoryKey
LEFT JOIN (SELECT GLAcctKey, MAX(FiscYear) AS LastFiscYear, COUNT(*) AS Periods
           FROM   tglAcctHist
           WHERE  DebitAmt <> 0 OR CreditAmt <> 0
           GROUP BY GLAcctKey) act ON act.GLAcctKey = a.GLAcctKey
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS'
ORDER BY a.GLAcctNo;

-- 2b. Account + reference code combinations actually posted (input to the
--     Sage-to-Fusion account mapping). A NULL AcctRef means no reference code.
SELECT RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo) AS GLAcctNo, RTRIM(a.Description) AS AcctDesc,
       RTRIM(r.AcctRefCode) AS AcctRef, RTRIM(r.Description) AS AcctRefDesc,
       COUNT(*) AS Lines, SUM(t.PostAmtHC) AS NetAmt
FROM   tglTransaction t
JOIN   tglAccount a      ON a.GLAcctKey = t.GLAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tglAcctRef r   ON r.AcctRefKey = t.AcctRefKey
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND t.FiscYear = '2027'
GROUP BY a.GLAcctNo, a.Description, r.AcctRefCode, r.Description
ORDER BY a.GLAcctNo, r.AcctRefCode;

-- 2c. Fiscal calendar. Map periods by date, never by number.
SELECT FiscYear, FiscPer, CONVERT(varchar(10), StartDate, 120) AS StartDate,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), EndDate, 120) AS EndDate, Status   -- 1 Open, 2 Closed
FROM   tglFiscalPeriod
WHERE  CompanyID = 'BDS' AND FiscYear >= '2024'
ORDER BY FiscYear, FiscPer;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   3. TRIAL BALANCE
   BegBal is populated in period 1 only. Ending balance is the period-1 opening
   balance plus cumulative net activity. Total must be 0.000.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo) AS GLAcctNo, RTRIM(a.Description) AS Description,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.FiscPer = 1 THEN h.BegBal ELSE 0 END)              AS OpeningBal,
       SUM(h.DebitAmt)                                                    AS Debits,
       SUM(h.CreditAmt)                                                   AS Credits,
       SUM(CASE WHEN h.FiscPer = 1 THEN h.BegBal ELSE 0 END)
         + SUM(h.DebitAmt - h.CreditAmt)                                  AS EndingBal
FROM   tglAcctHist h
JOIN   tglAccount a ON a.GLAcctKey = h.GLAcctKey
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS'
  AND  h.FiscYear = '2027'
  AND  h.FiscPer <= 8
GROUP BY a.GLAcctNo, a.Description
HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN h.FiscPer = 1 THEN h.BegBal ELSE 0 END)
         + SUM(h.DebitAmt - h.CreditAmt) <> 0
ORDER BY a.GLAcctNo;

-- 3b. Integrity: activity in the journal lines equals activity in the balances
SELECT (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN t.PostAmtHC > 0 THEN t.PostAmtHC ELSE 0 END)
        FROM tglTransaction t JOIN tglAccount a ON a.GLAcctKey = t.GLAcctKey
        WHERE a.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND t.FiscYear = '2027' AND t.FiscPer = 7) AS JournalDebits,
       (SELECT SUM(h.DebitAmt)
        FROM tglAcctHist h JOIN tglAccount a ON a.GLAcctKey = h.GLAcctKey
        WHERE a.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND h.FiscYear = '2027' AND h.FiscPer = 7) AS BalanceDebits;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   4. GENERAL LEDGER DETAIL
   Positive PostAmtHC is a debit. Always filter FiscYear first: 29.9M rows.
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT t.glTranKey,
       RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo)     AS GLAcctNo,
       RTRIM(r.AcctRefCode)  AS AcctRef,
       t.FiscYear, t.FiscPer,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), t.PostDate, 120) AS PostDate,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), t.TranDate, 120) AS TranDate,
       RTRIM(d.ModuleID)     AS SourceModule,
       t.TranType, RTRIM(ls.LocalText) AS TranTypeDesc,
       RTRIM(t.TranNo)       AS TranNo,
       t.TranKey,                                   -- key of the source document
       RTRIM(j.JrnlID)       AS Journal, t.JrnlNo,
       RTRIM(b.BatchID)      AS BatchID, RTRIM(b.PostUserID) AS PostedBy,
       t.PostAmtHC,
       t.PostCmnt
FROM   tglTransaction t
JOIN   tglAccount a          ON a.GLAcctKey = t.GLAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tglAcctRef r       ON r.AcctRefKey = t.AcctRefKey
LEFT JOIN tsmModuleDef d     ON d.ModuleNo = t.SourceModuleNo
LEFT JOIN tciTranType tt     ON tt.TranType = t.TranType
LEFT JOIN tsmLocalString ls  ON ls.StringNo = tt.TranDescStrNo AND ls.LanguageID = 1033
LEFT JOIN tglJournal j       ON j.JrnlKey = t.JrnlKey
LEFT JOIN tciBatchLog b      ON b.BatchKey = t.BatchKey
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS'
  AND  t.FiscYear = '2027' AND t.FiscPer = 8
  AND  a.GLAcctNo = '200000'
ORDER BY t.glTranKey;

-- 4b. Where the ledger's volume comes from (sizes the post-cut-over bridge)
SELECT RTRIM(d.ModuleID) AS SourceModule, t.TranType, RTRIM(ls.LocalText) AS TranTypeDesc,
       COUNT(*) AS Lines,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.PostAmtHC > 0 THEN t.PostAmtHC ELSE 0 END) AS Debits
FROM   tglTransaction t
JOIN   tglAccount a          ON a.GLAcctKey = t.GLAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tsmModuleDef d     ON d.ModuleNo = t.SourceModuleNo
LEFT JOIN tciTranType tt     ON tt.TranType = t.TranType
LEFT JOIN tsmLocalString ls  ON ls.StringNo = tt.TranDescStrNo AND ls.LanguageID = 1033
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND t.FiscYear = '2027'
GROUP BY d.ModuleID, t.TranType, ls.LocalText
ORDER BY Lines DESC;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   5. ACCOUNTS PAYABLE
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- 5a. Supplier conversion candidates: active in the window or holding open items.
--     Bank and tax columns are deliberately left out; add them only for the
--     controlled supplier-bank extract.
SELECT v.VendKey, RTRIM(v.VendID) AS VendID, RTRIM(v.VendName) AS VendName,
       RTRIM(v.VendDBA) AS VendDBA, v.Status,
       RTRIM(vc.VendClassID) AS VendClass,
       RTRIM(pt.PmtTermsID)  AS PmtTerms,
       RTRIM(pm.VendPmtMethID) AS PmtMethod,
       v.V1099Type, RTRIM(v.V1099Form) AS V1099Form, RTRIM(v.V1099Box) AS V1099Box,
       v.HoldPmt,
       RTRIM(v.UserFld1) AS BusinessType,
       act.Vouchers24m, CONVERT(varchar(10), act.LastVoucher, 120) AS LastVoucher,
       ISNULL(op.OpenDocs, 0) AS OpenDocs, ISNULL(op.OpenBal, 0) AS OpenBal
FROM   tapVendor v
LEFT JOIN tapVendClass vc     ON vc.VendClassKey = v.VendClassKey
LEFT JOIN tciPaymentTerms pt  ON pt.PmtTermsKey = v.PmtTermsKey
LEFT JOIN tapVendPmtMethod pm ON pm.VendPmtMethKey = v.VendPmtMethKey
LEFT JOIN (SELECT VendKey, COUNT(*) AS Vouchers24m, MAX(TranDate) AS LastVoucher
           FROM   tapVoucher
           WHERE  TranDate >= '2024-11-01' AND TranDate < '2027-01-01'
           GROUP BY VendKey) act ON act.VendKey = v.VendKey
LEFT JOIN (SELECT VendKey, COUNT(*) AS OpenDocs, SUM(BalanceHC) AS OpenBal
           FROM   tapVoucher WHERE Status = 1
           GROUP BY VendKey) op ON op.VendKey = v.VendKey
WHERE  v.CompanyID = 'BDS'
  AND  (act.VendKey IS NOT NULL OR op.VendKey IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY v.VendID;

-- 5b. Supplier addresses (purchasing and remit-to) for those suppliers
SELECT v.VendKey, RTRIM(v.VendID) AS VendID, RTRIM(va.VendAddrID) AS VendAddrID,
       CASE WHEN va.AddrKey = v.DfltPurchAddrKey   THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IsDefaultPurchasing,
       CASE WHEN va.AddrKey = v.DfltRemitToAddrKey THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS IsDefaultRemitTo,
       RTRIM(ad.AddrName) AS AddrName, RTRIM(ad.AddrLine1) AS AddrLine1,
       RTRIM(ad.AddrLine2) AS AddrLine2, RTRIM(ad.City) AS City,
       RTRIM(ad.StateID) AS StateID, RTRIM(ad.PostalCode) AS PostalCode,
       RTRIM(ad.CountryID) AS CountryID,
       CASE WHEN RTRIM(ISNULL(va.BankAcctNo, '')) <> '' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS HasBankDetails
FROM   tapVendor v
JOIN   tapVendAddr va ON va.VendKey = v.VendKey
JOIN   tciAddress ad  ON ad.AddrKey = va.AddrKey
WHERE  v.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND v.Status = 1
ORDER BY v.VendID, va.VendAddrID;

-- 5c. Open payables, aged from DueDate as of a stated date
SELECT RTRIM(v.VendID) AS VendID, RTRIM(v.VendName) AS VendName,
       vo.VoucherKey,
       RTRIM(vo.TranNo)  AS SupplierInvoiceNo,
       RTRIM(vo.VouchNo) AS SageVoucherNo,
       RTRIM(ttc.TranTypeID) AS DocType,           -- IN invoice, DM debit memo
       CONVERT(varchar(10), vo.TranDate, 120) AS InvoiceDate,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), vo.DueDate, 120)  AS DueDate,
       RTRIM(pt.PmtTermsID) AS PmtTerms,
       vo.TranAmtHC AS OriginalAmt, vo.BalanceHC AS OpenAmt,
       vo.HoldPmt,
       RTRIM(vc.VendClassID) AS VendClass,
       RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo) AS APControlAcct,
       CASE WHEN vo.DueDate >= '2026-11-13' THEN 'Current'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, vo.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 30 THEN '1-30'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, vo.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 60 THEN '31-60'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, vo.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 90 THEN '61-90'
            ELSE 'Over 90' END AS AgeBucket
FROM   tapVoucher vo
JOIN   tapVendor v              ON v.VendKey = vo.VendKey
LEFT JOIN tapVendClass vc       ON vc.VendClassKey = vo.VendClassKey
LEFT JOIN tglAccount a          ON a.GLAcctKey = vc.AcctsPaybleAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tciPaymentTerms pt    ON pt.PmtTermsKey = vo.PmtTermsKey
LEFT JOIN tciTranTypeCompany ttc ON ttc.CompanyID = vo.CompanyID AND ttc.TranType = vo.TranType
WHERE  vo.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND vo.Status = 1
ORDER BY v.VendID, vo.DueDate;

-- 5d. AP subledger to GL, by control account. Variance must be 0.
SELECT s.APControlAcct, s.OpenDocs, s.SubledgerBal, -g.GLBal AS GLBal,
       s.SubledgerBal + g.GLBal AS Variance
FROM  (SELECT RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo) AS APControlAcct, a.GLAcctKey,
              COUNT(*) AS OpenDocs, SUM(vo.BalanceHC) AS SubledgerBal
       FROM   tapVoucher vo
       JOIN   tapVendClass vc ON vc.VendClassKey = vo.VendClassKey
       JOIN   tglAccount a    ON a.GLAcctKey = vc.AcctsPaybleAcctKey
       WHERE  vo.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND vo.Status = 1
       GROUP BY a.GLAcctNo, a.GLAcctKey) s
JOIN  (SELECT h.GLAcctKey,
              SUM(CASE WHEN h.FiscPer = 1 THEN h.BegBal ELSE 0 END)
                + SUM(h.DebitAmt - h.CreditAmt) AS GLBal
       FROM   tglAcctHist h
       WHERE  h.FiscYear = '2027' AND h.FiscPer <= 8
       GROUP BY h.GLAcctKey) g ON g.GLAcctKey = s.GLAcctKey;
-- Note: an expense account used as a class "control" account (600500 for class
-- Int Tech) will show a variance by nature; only true liability accounts tie.

-- 5e. Payment history for one supplier
SELECT RTRIM(p.TranID) AS PaymentID, RTRIM(ttc.TranTypeID) AS PmtType,   -- CK, EF, OT
       CONVERT(varchar(10), p.TranDate, 120) AS PmtDate, p.TranAmtHC AS PmtAmt,
       RTRIM(ap.ApplyToTranID) AS AppliedToInvoice, ap.PmtAmtHC AS AppliedAmt,
       ap.DiscTakenAmtHC AS DiscountTaken
FROM   tapVendPmt p
JOIN   tapVendor v              ON v.VendKey = p.VendKey
LEFT JOIN tapVendPmtAppl ap     ON ap.ApplyFromPmtKey = p.VendPmtKey
LEFT JOIN tciTranTypeCompany ttc ON ttc.CompanyID = p.CompanyID AND ttc.TranType = p.TranType
WHERE  p.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND v.VendID = 'Stratix'
  AND  p.TranDate >= '2026-04-01'
ORDER BY p.TranDate, p.TranID;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   6. ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- 6a. Customers that are actually billed, with their national account
SELECT c.CustKey, RTRIM(c.CustID) AS CustID, RTRIM(c.CustName) AS CustName, c.Status,
       RTRIM(cc.CustClassID) AS CustClass,
       RTRIM(na.NationalAcctID) AS NationalAcctID, RTRIM(na.Description) AS NationalAcct,
       act.Invoices24m, act.Billed24m, CONVERT(varchar(10), act.LastInvoice, 120) AS LastInvoice,
       ISNULL(op.OpenDocs, 0) AS OpenDocs, ISNULL(op.OpenBal, 0) AS OpenBal
FROM   tarCustomer c
LEFT JOIN tarCustClass cc            ON cc.CustClassKey = c.CustClassKey
LEFT JOIN tarNationalAcctLevel nal   ON nal.NationalAcctLevelKey = c.NationalAcctLevelKey
LEFT JOIN tarNationalAcct na         ON na.NationalAcctKey = nal.NationalAcctKey
LEFT JOIN (SELECT CustKey, COUNT(*) AS Invoices24m, SUM(TranAmtHC) AS Billed24m,
                  MAX(TranDate) AS LastInvoice
           FROM   tarInvoice
           WHERE  TranDate >= '2024-11-01' AND Status <> 3
           GROUP BY CustKey) act ON act.CustKey = c.CustKey
LEFT JOIN (SELECT CustKey, COUNT(*) AS OpenDocs, SUM(BalanceHC) AS OpenBal
           FROM   tarInvoice WHERE Status = 1
           GROUP BY CustKey) op ON op.CustKey = c.CustKey
WHERE  c.CompanyID = 'BDS'
  AND  (act.CustKey IS NOT NULL OR op.CustKey IS NOT NULL)
ORDER BY act.Billed24m DESC;

-- 6b. Open receivables, aged from DueDate as of a stated date
SELECT RTRIM(c.CustID) AS CustID, RTRIM(c.CustName) AS CustName,
       i.InvcKey, RTRIM(i.TranID) AS InvoiceNo,
       RTRIM(ttc.TranTypeID) AS DocType,           -- IN invoice, CM credit memo
       CONVERT(varchar(10), i.TranDate, 120) AS InvoiceDate,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), i.DueDate, 120)  AS DueDate,
       RTRIM(i.CustPONo) AS CustPONo,
       RTRIM(pt.PmtTermsID) AS PmtTerms,
       i.TranAmtHC AS OriginalAmt, i.BalanceHC AS OpenAmt,
       i.SalesAmt, i.STaxAmt, i.ShipAmt,
       RTRIM(cc.CustClassID) AS CustClass,
       CASE WHEN i.DueDate >= '2026-11-13' THEN 'Current'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, i.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 30 THEN '1-30'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, i.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 60 THEN '31-60'
            WHEN DATEDIFF(day, i.DueDate, '2026-11-13') <= 90 THEN '61-90'
            ELSE 'Over 90' END AS AgeBucket
FROM   tarInvoice i
JOIN   tarCustomer c            ON c.CustKey = i.CustKey
LEFT JOIN tarCustClass cc       ON cc.CustClassKey = i.CustClassKey
LEFT JOIN tciPaymentTerms pt    ON pt.PmtTermsKey = i.PmtTermsKey
LEFT JOIN tciTranTypeCompany ttc ON ttc.CompanyID = i.CompanyID AND ttc.TranType = i.TranType
WHERE  i.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND i.Status = 1
ORDER BY c.CustID, i.DueDate;

-- 6c. Unapplied receipts
SELECT RTRIM(c.CustID) AS CustID, RTRIM(c.CustName) AS CustName,
       RTRIM(p.TranID) AS ReceiptID, CONVERT(varchar(10), p.TranDate, 120) AS ReceiptDate,
       p.TranAmtHC AS ReceiptAmt, p.UnappliedAmtHC AS UnappliedAmt
FROM   tarCustPmt p
JOIN   tarCustomer c ON c.CustKey = p.CustKey
WHERE  p.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND p.UnappliedAmtHC <> 0
ORDER BY p.UnappliedAmtHC DESC;

-- 6d. AR subledger to GL. Snapshot result: subledger 910,725.16 above GL.
SELECT s.OpenInvoices, s.OpenInvoiceBal, u.UnappliedReceipts, u.UnappliedBal,
       s.OpenInvoiceBal - u.UnappliedBal AS SubledgerNet,
       g.GLBal,
       s.OpenInvoiceBal - u.UnappliedBal - g.GLBal AS Variance
FROM  (SELECT COUNT(*) AS OpenInvoices, SUM(BalanceHC) AS OpenInvoiceBal
       FROM   tarInvoice WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1) s
CROSS JOIN
      (SELECT COUNT(*) AS UnappliedReceipts, ISNULL(SUM(UnappliedAmtHC), 0) AS UnappliedBal
       FROM   tarCustPmt WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND UnappliedAmtHC <> 0) u
CROSS JOIN
      (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN h.FiscPer = 1 THEN h.BegBal ELSE 0 END)
                + SUM(h.DebitAmt - h.CreditAmt) AS GLBal
       FROM   tglAcctHist h
       WHERE  h.FiscYear = '2027' AND h.FiscPer <= 8
         AND  h.GLAcctKey IN (SELECT AcctsRecAcctKey FROM tarCustClass WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS')) g;

-- 6e. Postings to the AR control account that did not come from AR
--     (first place to look for the variance)
SELECT RTRIM(d.ModuleID) AS SourceModule, t.TranType, t.FiscYear,
       COUNT(*) AS Lines, SUM(t.PostAmtHC) AS NetAmt
FROM   tglTransaction t
JOIN   tglAccount a      ON a.GLAcctKey = t.GLAcctKey
LEFT JOIN tsmModuleDef d ON d.ModuleNo = t.SourceModuleNo
WHERE  a.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND a.GLAcctNo = '101000'
  AND  t.SourceModuleNo <> 5
GROUP BY d.ModuleID, t.TranType, t.FiscYear
ORDER BY t.FiscYear, SourceModule;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   7. CASH
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- 7a. Cash accounts and their GL accounts (bank numbers deliberately omitted)
SELECT ca.CashAcctKey, RTRIM(ca.CashAcctID) AS CashAcctID, RTRIM(ca.Description) AS Description,
       RTRIM(b.BankID) AS BankID, RTRIM(ca.CurrID) AS CurrID,
       RTRIM(a.GLAcctNo) AS GLAcctNo, ca.CurntBal
FROM   tcmCashAcct ca
LEFT JOIN tcmBank b    ON b.BankKey = ca.BankKey
LEFT JOIN tglAccount a ON a.GLAcctKey = ca.GLAcctKey
WHERE  ca.CompanyID = 'BDS';

-- 7b. Outstanding (uncleared) cash transactions
SELECT RTRIM(ca.CashAcctID) AS CashAcctID, ct.TranType,
       COUNT(*) AS Items, SUM(ct.TranAmtHC) AS Amount,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), MIN(ct.TranDate), 120) AS Oldest
FROM   tcmCashTran ct
JOIN   tcmCashAcct ca ON ca.CashAcctKey = ct.CashAcctKey
WHERE  ct.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND ct.Status = 1
GROUP BY ca.CashAcctID, ct.TranType
ORDER BY ca.CashAcctID, ct.TranType;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   8. CONVERSION SCOPE COUNTS (re-run on the cut-over copy)
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT 'GL accounts'                AS Measure, COUNT(*) AS N FROM tglAccount WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'GL accounts active',          COUNT(*) FROM tglAccount WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1
UNION ALL SELECT 'Account reference codes',     COUNT(*) FROM tglAcctRef WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Suppliers',                   COUNT(*) FROM tapVendor WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Suppliers active',            COUNT(*) FROM tapVendor WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1
UNION ALL SELECT 'Suppliers 1099 active',       COUNT(*) FROM tapVendor WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1 AND V1099Type IN (1, 2)
UNION ALL SELECT 'Open AP documents',           COUNT(*) FROM tapVoucher WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1
UNION ALL SELECT 'Unposted vouchers',           COUNT(*) FROM tapPendVoucher WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Customers',                   COUNT(*) FROM tarCustomer WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Customers active',            COUNT(*) FROM tarCustomer WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1
UNION ALL SELECT 'National accounts',           COUNT(*) FROM tarNationalAcct WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Open AR documents',           COUNT(*) FROM tarInvoice WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND Status = 1
UNION ALL SELECT 'Unposted invoices',           COUNT(*) FROM tarPendInvoice WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Unapplied receipts',          COUNT(*) FROM tarCustPmt WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND UnappliedAmtHC <> 0
UNION ALL SELECT 'Cash accounts',               COUNT(*) FROM tcmCashAcct WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Payment terms',               COUNT(*) FROM tciPaymentTerms WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS'
UNION ALL SELECT 'Open projects',               COUNT(*) FROM tPA00175 WHERE CompanyID = 'BDS' AND OpenOrClosed = 1;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   9. CUSTOM OBJECT REVIEW (catalog only; module source is not readable here)
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
-- 9a. Install and upgrade waves. Objects created on other days are suspects.
SELECT CONVERT(date, create_date) AS CreatedOn,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'U'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Tables,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'V'  THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Views,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'TR' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Triggers,
       SUM(CASE WHEN type IN ('P', 'FN', 'IF', 'TF') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS Code
FROM   sys.objects
WHERE  is_ms_shipped = 0 AND type IN ('U', 'V', 'P', 'FN', 'IF', 'TF', 'TR')
GROUP BY CONVERT(date, create_date)
HAVING COUNT(*) >= 15
ORDER BY CreatedOn;

-- 9b. Objects carrying an author tag, with size and last change
SELECT o.type_desc, o.name,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), o.create_date, 120) AS Created,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), o.modify_date, 120) AS Modified,
       (SELECT SUM(p.rows) FROM sys.partitions p
        WHERE p.object_id = o.object_id AND p.index_id IN (0, 1)) AS RowCnt
FROM   sys.objects o
WHERE  o.is_ms_shipped = 0
  AND  o.type IN ('U', 'V', 'P', 'FN', 'IF', 'TF')
  AND (o.name LIKE '%BW%'     OR o.name LIKE '%bwick%'  OR o.name LIKE '%[_]RKL%'
    OR o.name LIKE '%[_]SSS%' OR o.name LIKE '%MAG%'    OR o.name LIKE '%[_]ERP%'
    OR o.name LIKE '%exactor%' OR o.name LIKE '%[_]BDS' OR o.name LIKE '%XPNS%'
    OR o.name LIKE '%Modula%' OR o.name LIKE '%Adaptive%')
ORDER BY o.type_desc, o.name;

-- 9c. Views and tables created outside the install waves (untagged custom work)
SELECT o.type_desc, o.name,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), o.create_date, 120) AS Created,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), o.modify_date, 120) AS Modified
FROM   sys.objects o
WHERE  o.is_ms_shipped = 0 AND o.type IN ('U', 'V')
  AND  CONVERT(date, o.create_date) NOT IN
       ('2005-04-26', '2006-11-12', '2008-07-26', '2008-07-27', '2013-12-27', '2013-12-28',
        '2015-03-27', '2015-06-30', '2019-04-05', '2019-04-06', '2020-07-14', '2025-02-18')
ORDER BY o.create_date;

-- 9d. Triggers created outside the install waves. Sage's own triggers
--     (tI_/tU_/tD_<table>, ..._DBAudit, ..._AppAudit) were all rebuilt on
--     2019-04-05/06, and the 2006 warehouse add-on's on 2006-11-12, so what
--     remains is custom. Name-based filters do not work: there are 3,420.
SELECT tr.name AS TriggerName, OBJECT_NAME(tr.parent_id) AS TableName, tr.is_disabled,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), tr.create_date, 120) AS Created
FROM   sys.triggers tr
WHERE  tr.parent_class = 1
  AND  CONVERT(date, tr.create_date) NOT IN ('2006-11-12', '2019-04-05', '2019-04-06')
ORDER BY tr.create_date;

-- 9e. External dependencies: every synonym and where it points
SELECT name AS SynonymName, base_object_name AS Target,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), create_date, 120) AS Created
FROM   sys.synonyms
ORDER BY base_object_name;

-- 9f. User-defined fields in use, by host table
SELECT RTRIM(e.HostTableName) AS HostTable, u.UserFldNo, RTRIM(u.Title) AS Title
FROM   tciUserField u
JOIN   tciEntity e ON e.EntityType = u.EntityType
WHERE  u.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND RTRIM(u.Title) NOT IN ('', 'Not Used')
ORDER BY e.HostTableName, u.UserFldNo;

-- 9g. Customised screens
SELECT RTRIM(f.FormName) AS FormName, f.CompanyID, f.CustomFormEnabled,
       RTRIM(f.UserID) AS OnlyForUser,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tsmCustomFormDetl d WHERE d.CustomFormKey = f.CustomFormKey) AS ControlsChanged
FROM   tsmCustomForm f
ORDER BY ControlsChanged DESC;

-- 9h. Is an interface still alive? Latest entry in each custom log.
SELECT 'Concur file log' AS Interface, COUNT(*) AS Entries,
       CONVERT(varchar(10), MAX(DownloadDate), 120) AS Latest FROM tpaConcurLog_rkl
UNION ALL SELECT 'RKL integration log', COUNT(*), CONVERT(varchar(10), MAX(CreateDate), 120) FROM tciIntegrationLog_RKL
UNION ALL SELECT 'Exactor sales tax',   COUNT(*), CONVERT(varchar(10), MAX(SalesDate), 120)  FROM exactor_transaction
UNION ALL SELECT 'Master-data audit',   COUNT(*), CONVERT(varchar(10), MAX(SysDate), 120)    FROM tciMaintAuditLog;


/* ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   10. PROJECTS (context for open AR and AP; later leg)
   --------------------------------------------------------------------------- */
SELECT RTRIM(mp.chrMasterJobNumber) AS MasterProject, RTRIM(p.chrJobNumber) AS Project,
       RTRIM(p.chrJobName) AS ProjectName, RTRIM(c.CustID) AS CustID,
       p.OpenOrClosed,                               -- 1 Open, 2 Closed
       CONVERT(varchar(10), p.dteJobCommencement, 120) AS StartDate,
       p.numJTDActualCost AS ActualCost, p.numJTDActualSale AS ActualSales,
       p.numJTDCommitedCsts AS CommittedCost
FROM   tPA00175 p
LEFT JOIN tPA00176 mp   ON mp.intMasterJobKey = p.intMasterJobKey
LEFT JOIN tarCustomer c ON c.CustKey = p.CustKey
WHERE  p.CompanyID = 'BDS' AND p.OpenOrClosed = 1
ORDER BY mp.chrMasterJobNumber, p.chrJobNumber;
```
